messages:
maria: Proposing a small design spike — 'filter sculpting' for the console query bar. Goal: let PMs/SEs quickly compose per-route + per-model comparisons without saving lots of ephemeral savedviews.

dan: Love the name. Can you sketch the flows? are we talking ad-hoc compare or a persistent mini-view?

maria: Ad-hoc by default. Two modes: Quick-sculpt (temporary, one-click compare) and Pin-as-saved (promote to saved query). Keeps console uncluttered.

sam: UX idea: a floating panel that shows active clauses + a live traffic preview (sample rate). Users can drag clauses to create OR groups.

lee: Frontend constraints: dragging + live sample = we need a compact diff protocol. Recomputing telemetry on every drag could be heavy. How frequent are the updates?

maria: Default live preview: throttle to 1s, sampling window = last 1h by default. We can expose controls for sample size.

dan: API changes: we should avoid adding a new expensive endpoint. Suggest reusing /api/console/route-query with a query profile header: `x-console-sculpt: true`. Server returns a small sample+counts instead of full telemetry. Example response: 
```
{
  sample_count: 200,
  matches: 42,
  token_avg: 12.3,
  latency_p50: 120
}
```

maria: That sample payload is perfect — small and UI-friendly. Also need support for model-scoped clauses: e.g., `model:gh-llama2, route:/search` semantics.

lee: We should add a canonical, stable serialization for sculpt rules so a pinned result can be shared. Maybe `sculpt=q:(route=/search; model=gh-llama2; tokens>50)` in the URL. No nested json in querystring.

dan: Agree. On the server side we'll parse that into the existing query planner. But watch out for quota/telemetry costs: if people run 1s throttle with large sample windows we could flood telemetry ingestion.

ops-bot: NOTE: Current per-route telemetry retention is 7d for detailed samples. Any ad-hoc increase will require a quota adjustment ticket.

maria: Good call. Proposal: quick-sculpt uses low-fidelity sampling (200 events) and counts only. Pin-as-saved can trigger a readability job that uses full fidelity but runs async and stores results.

dan: Implementation plan for rollout: 1) API shim that accepts `x-console-sculpt` and returns sample payload (beta). 2) Frontend floating panel + throttle. 3) Pin flow to create saved-query via existing savedqueries API. 4) Gradual rollout to 10% of orgs.

lee: For the floating UI, will need an accessibility pass. Also allow keyboard quick-add for clauses.

sam: One more UX ask: show signal-to-noise indicator on the preview (low sample -> warn: noisy).

maria: Good. I'll write a short product brief and include the `sculpt` serialization. Dan/Lee can pair for the API+panel spike next week.

dan: I'll open a prelim PR for the API header and minimal sample endpoint. Assigning to @lee for frontend.

ops-bot: Created ticket #CI-4291 for telemetry quota review.

maria: Thanks — will sync in sprint planning tomorrow. :rocket:
